text: Describe a time when you prioritized user experience in a technical decision.
primary_rendered:
QUESTION (Impact & Long-Term Vision): Describe a time when you prioritized user experience in a technical decision.

[PRIMARY] EX-01 | Search Diversity --- Intent Collapse via Item-vs-Page Diagnosis
  situation: During Hacker Week I went looking for where our search ranker was failing silently. Standard dashboards looked healthy. But multi-intent queries like "pokemon" returned 90%+ trading cards, while purchase data showed half the buyers wanted games, toys, or figures. The dashboard was fine because the dominant-intent users were fine. The missing half was invisible.
  task: No one had assigned this. One week to go from a hunch to a defensible diagnosis plus a working prototype -- or drop it. The framing mattered more than the fix. If I couldn't name precisely why the ranker produced homogeneous pages, nobody downstream would fund a multi-intent solution on top of a hea
  action: First pass: abandon-log slice. Sorted queries by post-impression drop-off and looked for the pattern. Hundreds of high-volume multi-intent queries collapsed the same way -- one product type crowded out every other valid interpretation. Not a bug on any single query. A systematic bias.  Root-cause call: the ranker scored each item in isolation. It had no mechanism to reason about the page. When the top candidates all looked alike, the page looked alike -- by design. Item-level scoring was producing page-level homogeneity, and no amount of per-item tuning would fix it. The gap was structural, no
  result: The prototype survived review and grew past Hacker Week. Compounded across verticals into 200M+ annualized impact over multiple years. The methodology was later written up at SIGIR.  The lesson I carry: **item-level scoring creates page-level homogeneity.** Any time a ranker optimizes per-candidate without a page-level constraint, the top-K will cluster -- and the dashboard will look fine because 
  evidence_quotes: ["pokemon → 结果几乎全是 TCG card，但用户实际购买 ~50% 是 games / toys / figures / 周边", "项目从未被指派，完全由自己发现、推动、跨 team 落地"]
  cn_elevator_pitch: Hacker Week 自己去找 search ranker 在哪 silently failing -- dashboard 显示健康但 multi-intent query 比如 "pokemon" 90%+ 返回 trading cards，而购买数据显示一半 buyer 要 games / toys / figures；abandon-log slice 发现上百个 high-volume query 同样 collapse，根因不在 per-item calibration 而在 ranker 按 item 独立打分没有 page-level reasoning -- item-le

probe_notes.core_signal: 这题本质在问: 在做技术决策时, 是把 surface-level metrics 当作 proxy 还是把真实用户 pain 当作锚点。L5 bar 是能识别出 'metrics 健康但用户体验受损' 的系统性 bias, 并主动 drive 一个没有 explicit ownership 的 initiative 来修复它。
what_good_looks_like: 显式引用 EX-01 primary 动作: 'Sorted queries by post-impression drop-off' -- 从用户离开信号反推不可见的需求, 而不是靠 dashboard 说故事。
用户 pain 有 concrete evidence: '购买数据显示一半的 buyer 要的是 games / toys / figures, 但首页全都是 trading cards' -- 数据对数据, 不靠直觉。
技术决策的 causal chain 清晰: item-level scoring → page-level homogeneity → 用户 choice collapse -- 点明 structural 缺陷, 不是简单的 '加几个 feature'。
Impact 有 long-term 视角: 不是单次 query fix, 而是 cross-vertical 落地, 最终变成 page-level 的 ranking 约束, 并且方法论沉淀为 SIGIR 论文。
what_L5_adds: 从 'metrics 没问题' 到 'user pain 被 dominant intent 掩盖' 的 diagnosis frame shift -- 这是 L5 的 system-thinking, 不是在给已有的 alert 做响应。
Proactive ownership: 项目从未被指派, 完全自驱, 体现了对用户体验的 personal commitment, 而非等 product ticket 或 outage 推动。
Long-term architectural vision: 把 fix 从 per-item tuning 升级为 page-level constraint, 让后续所有 vertical 受益 -- 这是 org-level influence, 而非 local optimization。
common_failure_modes: 技术决策纯讲 metric uplift, 没有 user pain evidence: 比如只说 '优化了 NDCG 提升了 +2%', 不说对 real user 意味着什么 -- reviewer 会认为只是在跑实验。
把 dashboard 健康当终点: 不去质疑 metrics 是否 cover 了所有用户群体, 直接停在表面 -- 缺乏 L5 应有的 critical thinking。
只接 ticket, 不主动 identify opportunity: 如果 story 的触发点是 PM 或 manager 指派的, 就失去了自驱 ownership 的信号。
解决方案是 incremental tuning: '加了几个 diversity signal' 或 '调了 weight', 没有触及 structural design (item vs page) 的 root cause -- reviewer 会认为 impact 不可持续。

text: How do you balance technical debt with feature delivery?
primary_rendered:
QUESTION (Impact & Long-Term Vision): How do you balance technical debt with feature delivery?

[PRIMARY] EX-21 | Tech Debt Balance --- Declarative Artifactory Proof of Concept
  situation: Features I was building required the team's new declarative artifactory system, but that system was repeatedly delayed with no clear timeline -- blocking feature delivery that the business needed now.
  task: Find a path that unblocks feature delivery without creating a throwaway workaround. Core question: which values of the declarative system can be captured now, so the work remains aligned with long-term architecture?
  action: - Deep research revealed the declarative system's architectural essence: the core value is generating a JSON ranking rule expression; the blockers were peripheral infrastructure (storage, versioning, deployment) -- not the expression generation itself - Designed approach using an internal caching system for storage, injecting named expressions as parameters into the search engine - Built parity tests proving hand-generated expressions were **identical** to what the declarative system's profiling layer would generate -- hard evidence, not promises - Demoed equivalence to the team; declarative t
  result: Feature **shipped on time** with business win, rather than being blocked for a year. When the declarative system finally became ready, migration was smooth -- the core expression implementation was already consistent, requiring only storage/versioning migration. The interim solution effectively became **early validation for the declarative system itself**. Key thesis: tech debt isn't a "fast vs. c
  evidence_quotes: ["Tech debt is not a fast-vs-clean binary --- it is whether you truly understand the system's architectural essence", "Identified boundary between core (named expr generation) and peripheral (storage/versioning/deployment infrastructure)", "Parity test provided hard evidence that hand-generated name
  cn_elevator_pitch: 新功能依赖团队 declarative artifactory 系统但长期 delay 无 timeline；深入研究发现核心价值是 JSON ranking rule expression generation，blocker 是周边 infra；用内部 caching 系统做 storage，功能按时交付且后续迁移无缝衔接 | KEY FACTS: 核心 vs 周边分离 | parity tests 验证一致性 | 按时交付 vs 等一年 | 迁移仅需 storage/versioning 切换

probe_notes.core_signal: 这题本质在问: 是否能在特性交付压力下仍守护 architectural integrity, 并证明技术债不是干净与否的二元选择题。L5 bar 是能从 fast vs clean 表面分歧中抽出 architectural essence, 并在阶段性交付中同时服务当前业务和长期架构。
what_good_looks_like: Framing 避免 binary: EX-21 primary 动作 'tech debt isn't a fast-vs-clean binary -- it is whether you truly understand the system's architectural essence' 直接定义了审题高度。
Concrete de-risking 证据: parity tests 证明 hand-written expression 与 declarative system 生成 identical -- 信用不是承诺给出来的, 是 traceable artefact 给出来的。
Long-term alignment 不空泛: 明确迁移仅需 'storage/versioning migration' 因为核心 expression 已对齐 -- 这是可检修的 alignment, 不是愿望。
First-person ownership: 不 blame declarative system team 的 delay, 反而把他们架构的核心 (JSON expression generation) 取出来提前验证, 把 external delay 转化成了 early validation 资产。
what_L5_adds: Org-level vision bleed: interim solution 不止 unblock 自己 feature, 它 'became early validation for the declarative system itself' -- L5 的 artifact 是给未来 org 用的, 不只是给自己用的。
Self-awareness around constraints: 系统 told me 核心已 ready / 周边还在建, 我没有重新发明 declarative system, 而是精准解耦 core from peripheral -- 这种 self-awareness 是 L5 级 engineering maturity。
Frame pivot from project to system evolution: L4 可能只答 'I found a workaround', L5 必须 show 这个 workaround 在架构演进图上占什么位置, 以及为什么它不是一次性的 hack 而是 phased delivery 的一步。
common_failure_modes: 讲成简单的 trade-off 模板: 'I paid some debt, built fast, later rewrote' -- 没有 architectural essence 的分析, reviewer 直接判断深度不足, 降级到 L4 以下。
Scapegoating external dependency: 'other team wasn't ready so I had no choice' -- 即使事实如此, 不 own 解耦方案的候选人会丢失 first-person 的 engineering authority, 典型的 ownership 信号断裂。
没有可追溯的验证: interim solution 不证明 long-term alignment, 只是说 'it worked fine' -- reviewer 看不到 traceability, 会怀疑 story 是编的或者技术含量低。
Redemption tail 过甜: '后来我的 hack 反而变成了正式方案' -- L5 bar 要的是 architectural phased delivery 的自然延伸, 不是意外惊喜的叙事, 后者暗示原计划没有 forward-looking intent, 会扣分。

text: Give an example of a project where you focused on long-term impact.
primary_rendered:
QUESTION (Impact & Long-Term Vision): Give an example of a project where you focused on long-term impact.

[PRIMARY] EX-06 | Allocation Framework as Reusable Platform Primitive — 200M+ Impact
  situation: Our initial diversity experiment showed +1% GMB, but I recognized the real opportunity was much larger -- other teams had similar under-exposure problems (authenticated listings, C2C new listings) that the same framework could solve.
  task: I needed to design the framework not as a one-off diversity solution, but as a reusable allocation primitive that other teams could plug into with minimal effort.
  action: - Designed the diversity solution not as a one-off fix but as a reusable allocation primitive: caching tables, deficit calculation pipeline, and uplift mechanism where new use cases only need to plug in a target distribution - Made a key architectural decision: unified GMB bidding dimension replacing the old LTR "scoring" paradigm with an ads-style "bidding + allocation" paradigm - This meant any ranking module (organic, carousel, ads) could compete in the same framework, eliminating the module proliferation problem
  result: The framework was reused for authenticated listings, C2C new listings, and other verticals -- each reuse delivered **+0.6%+ independent GMB gain**. Annualized total impact: **200M+**. The lesson: **platform primitive value far exceeds single optimization -- invest in hard infrastructure first.**
  evidence_quotes: ["框架的最大价值不是 diversity 本身，而是变成了一个可复用的 allocation primitive", "每次复用都能实现 0.6%+ 独立 GMB gain", "Platform primitive 的价值远大于单次优化"]
  cn_elevator_pitch: 从 diversity +1% GMB 单点实验识别出平台化机会；设计 reusable allocation primitive——caching + deficit calculation + uplift，替换 LTR scoring 为 ads-style bidding + allocation 范式 | KEY FACTS: reusable allocation primitive | ads-style bidding 范式 | 多 vertical 复用 +0.6%+ GMB | 200M+ annualized impact

OTHER LINKED STORIES (context only, 不必引用):
- BLOG-04 | Goal Tracking Reform: Honest Metrics Over Cosmetic Delivery: 团队 goal tracking 暗中奖励失败——改名、re-scope、rollover 伪装交付率；推动锁定 scope + peer confidence estimates，短期交付率下降反证系统生效 | KEY FACTS: 锁定 goal scope | peer confidence estimates 
- EX-01 | Search Diversity --- Intent Collapse via Item-vs-Page Diagnosis: Hacker Week 自己去找 search ranker 在哪 silently failing -- dashboard 显示健康但 multi-intent query 比如 "pokemon" 90%+ 返回 trading cards，而购买数据显示一半 buyer 要 games / toys / fig
- EX-33 | MoE -> Allocation Paradigm Shift - Org-Level Reframe via Honest Negative Result: eBay 搜索 org 范式停在 pairwise distributed ranking; leadership 批 MoE + neural ranking 项目 ~80 GPU nodes，我把 scope 定为 "start test" 而非 "test and launch"——放弃 carry-over 保
- EX-12B | Notebook -> ML Platform Migration --- Team Utilization 5% to 40% via Template+Profile Abstraction (Team-Cut of EX-12): 研究团队 notebook fleet 几百 GB memory reserved 但 utilization < 5%；几个 legacy R boosting 模型 (gbm 类) 无 refresh 通路、scale 不到 serving。先把 <5% 的 profile 数据摆在 leadership 和 RS

probe_notes.core_signal: 这题本质在问: 能否从 single-win 看到 platform leverage, 并愿意 invest hard infrastructure 即使短期收益更慢。L5 bar 是把单点优化 reframe 成 reusable primitive, 且能用具体 multi-vertical impact 证明长期判断, 而不止是 '我们做了个好东西, 别人也用了'。
what_good_looks_like: 开局 signal 清晰: 在 +1% GMB 的 diversity win 上, 主动 identify 'the real opportunity was much larger' -- 这是从 point solution 到 platform thinking 的 pivot, 你从第一天就在向长期看。

EX-06 primary 动作: 设计时直接选择 reusable allocation primitive, 把 caching tables / deficit calculation pipeline / uplift mechanism 抽象成 'new use cases only need to plug in a target distribution', 这是 invest in hard infrastructure 的具体契约。
Impact 分层量化: 不只讲总 200M+, 还能拆到每次复用 +0.6%+ independent GMB gain -- 这向 reviewer 证明长期价值是 traceable 的, 不是蹭运气。
Lesson 直接点出 mental model shift: 'platform primitive value far exceeds single optimization -- invest in hard infrastructure first', 这是 transferable 的 default, 不是项目总结。
what_L5_adds: 从 feature delivery 跃迁到 platform primitive design: 决策不是 '多做一个功能', 而是用 ads-style bidding + allocation 替换 LTR scoring 范式, 消除了 module proliferation 这类 org-level 摩擦, 这是 L5 才有的系统冲突诊断。
Org-level leverage 的自觉: 设计出来不是自己用, 是让 authenticated listings / C2C new listings 等团队 'plug in with minimal effort', 你在主动释放其他 team 的 capacity, 不是无意间帮到别人。
Self-awareness of trade-off: 愿意接受 infrastructure 的 upfront cost, 知道短期只有 diversity 但长期 each reuse delivers independent gain, 这种 delayed gratification 的叙事本身就是 L5 信号。
common_failure_modes: No platform thinking: 故事只在讲 one-off optimization 做得多好, 没有 why I chose to build it reusable / 没有 multi-team adoption 证据, reviewer 会判为 L4 以下执行者视角。
Impact 无分层: 只有总数字 '200M+', 不交代单个复用方增益 / 不交代复用数量, 会被认为在 pie-slice 蹭 org 整体增长, 不是我自己框架的因果。
Framework 是事后 patch: 如果听上去像先做了 diversity, 后来别人来要时再拆出来, 而不是 design-time 就决定, 会丧失 long-term vision 的主动性信号。
Lesson 停在项目级别: 'I learned that frameworks are good' -- 没有抽象成 mental model shift, L5 reviewer 无法判断我下次会怎么做, 当场降档。

text: Describe a time when you implemented an innovative solution.
primary_rendered:
QUESTION (Innovation & Strategic Thinking): Describe a time when you implemented an innovative solution.

[PRIMARY] EX-09 | Conversational Search — Proxy Item Breakthrough
  situation: In our LLM-powered conversational search project, query rewrites generated by the LLM consistently failed to find relevant results because the LLM's "world knowledge" didn't match our search engine's tokenizer and parser behavior -- plausible-sounding queries returned irrelevant or empty results.
  task: I needed to find a way to bridge the gap between LLM-generated intent and the existing search infrastructure, unblocking the project quickly.
  action: - Diagnosed the root cause: the LLM generated semantically correct queries, but the search engine's word segmentation and keyword interpretation mangled them into irrelevant results - Instead of fixing LLM query generation or retraining the search engine (both expensive, slow), discovered the proxy item approach: have the LLM generate descriptions of ideal items for each sub-intent, then use these as proxy items for ANN-based retrieval - This maximally leveraged existing infrastructure (embedding search, retrieval pipelines) with zero changes to the search engine - Each sub-intent got its own 
  result: The proxy item approach delivered strong results and was the **fastest path to unblocking experimentation**. It demonstrated maximum reuse of existing infrastructure while elegantly solving the LLM-search adaptation gap -- a solution that would have taken months via the alternatives.
  evidence_quotes: ["User: LLM的所谓world knowledge没有办法很好的adapt to我们的search", "User: 简单的传递keyword可能被我们的search engine误解并且断句断词得到不相关的结果", "User: 发现了proxy item得到了很好的结果，实现了对于已有infra和技术的最大程度利用和最快的test unblock"]
  cn_elevator_pitch: LLM query rewrite 因 tokenizer 不匹配持续返回无关结果；提出 proxy item 方案——让 LLM 生成理想商品描述再用向量匹配，最大化复用现有 infra 快速 unblock 实验 | KEY FACTS: LLM-search 适配鸿沟 | proxy item 方案 | 最大化现有 infra 复用 | 最快 unblock 路径

OTHER LINKED STORIES (context only, 不必引用):
- BLOG-03 | Cross-Org Boundary Defense via LLM Relevance Pipeline: Ads 团队要求共享 relevance 数据违反 org boundary；深挖发现真需求是验证 A/B 结果，构建 LLM relevance pipeline 日产 ~18K 标签 ~$500 替代人工标注 | KEY FACTS: ~18K 标签/天 ~$500 | 人工标注 $0.30-0.80/条 | or
- EX-14 | LLM Exploration --- Killing the Agentic Mandate with One Week of ROI Math: 2023 年 leadership 要 'upgrade to GenAI'，给 sandbox + API credits 自己探，没有 requirements、没有 LLM precedent；先用 1 周 feasibility 把 agentic search 路径用 ROI math 杀掉 -- 不能接 i
- EX-21 | Tech Debt Balance --- Declarative Artifactory Proof of Concept: 新功能依赖团队 declarative artifactory 系统但长期 delay 无 timeline；深入研究发现核心价值是 JSON ranking rule expression generation，blocker 是周边 infra；用内部 caching 系统做 storage，功能按时交付且后续迁移
- EX-01 | Search Diversity --- Intent Collapse via Item-vs-Page Diagnosis: Hacker Week 自己去找 search ranker 在哪 silently failing -- dashboard 显示健康但 multi-intent query 比如 "pokemon" 90%+ 返回 trading cards，而购买数据显示一半 buyer 要 games / toys / fig
- EX-09B | Conversational Search Privacy: Proxy Item Generation Eliminates Raw Query Leakage Risk (Privacy-Cut of EX-09): 在 LLM 对话搜索 design 阶段提出 query rewrite 路径会让用户原始 query 流入下游 log/训练数据的 privacy 风险；与 team 共同 develop proxy item 生成路径，让原始 query 永不流入下游，并把 privacy 优势写入 design doc | KE

probe_notes.core_signal: 这题本质在问: 在约束下找到非直觉的杠杆解, 且能解释为什么别人没看到这个解法。L5 bar 是把该解法抽象成可复制的 pattern, 并表明它改变了 org 对一类问题的解决方式。
what_good_looks_like: 清晰的 root cause 诊断: 不是泛泛说 '不 work', 而是 'LLM 的 world knowledge 与 search engine 的 tokenizer/parser 行为 mismatch' (如 EX-09 primary 动作)。
EX-09 primary 动作: 没有去修 LLM 或 retrain search engine (两者昂贵且慢), 而是发明 proxy item 路径 -- 让 LLM 生成理想 item 描述, 然后用现有 ANN 向量匹配检索, 零改动 infra。
Trade-off 显式: 能说清为什么其他方案被排除 -- '修 query 生成 cost 高 / retrain search engine 要数月', 而 proxy item '最快 unblock 实验'。
Downstream 与 leverage: 描述解决方案不仅是单点 fix, 还成为后续实验的基础, 且没有引入新 debt (比如 privacy 方面, 如 EX-09B 延伸, 但 primary 里已隐含)。
what_L5_adds: Pattern 抽象: 把 proxy item 定位为 'LLM 与遗留系统间的语义适配层', 这个抽象可以复用到其他 LLM 集成场景, 超越一次性的创新。
Org-level 成本视角: 展示了对替代方案的总成本评估 (LLM retraining / search engine 改造需要几个月 + 跨团队协调), 并证明自己方案的最大化复用 (zero changes to search engine) 是更优的 org-level 决策。
Influence through solution: 通过 fastest unblock 的 pitch 说服团队采用, 且无需 authority bring in -- 解法本身 self-evident, 体现 L5 的 'drive by leverage' 而非 push。
common_failure_modes: Aha moment 叙事: '我突然想到 proxy item 就好了' -- 缺少 root cause 诊断与 trade-off 推理, reviewer 会认为这个 innovation 是 luck 而非 systematic thinking。
不比选方案: 没有解释 '为什么别人没做 / 为什么之前没用这个方法', 无法展示 strategic constraint 下的 novelty, 感觉像一次普通 fix。
Impact 模糊: 只说 '结果很好' 而不具体 -- EX-09 里的 'fastest path to unblocking experimentation' 或 '数月的替代方案对比' 必须量化。
忽略风险/限制: 任何创新都有边界, 如 proxy item 对某些 sub-intent 可能不如精确 query rewrite。如果 candidate 不主动提 trade-off 或局限, reviewer 会担心 maturity 不足。

Diagnosis 停在 structural level, 不停止在 symptom: 把根因定在 'item-level scoring creates page-level homogeneity' -- 这是一个 design law, 不是 per-item tuning 问题。
低成本的最小原型验证: 一周之内从 hunch 到 defensible diagnosis + working prototype, 不先申请资源就 scale, 符合 self-starter 的 lean 逻辑。
Lesson 可跨 context 转移: 抽象出的 insight -- '任何 ranker 如果只管 per-candidate 最优, top-K 必然 cluster' -- 是可复现的 pattern, 不是只对一次查询有效。
what_L5_adds: 从单点发现抬到 class-level framing: 不仅解决 'pokemon' 查询, 而是识别出所有 multi-intent queries 的共性漏洞, 并最终跨 verticals 扩展, 把个人洞察变成 org capability。
挑战组织的隐藏假设: dashboard 显示健康, 因为你质疑了 'dominant-intent users 满意就代表全量健康' 这个前提, 独立定义了 'invisible missing half' -- 这是 strategic thinking 的核心信号。
长期复利和知识外溢: 影响 compounding 到 200M+ annualized, 且方法论沉淀成 SIGIR 论文, 表明 L5 会把自我驱动的项目变成 team 级别的学习资产。
common_failure_modes: 讲一个被分配的项目或 metric 优化: 缺乏 self-initiated 的起点, reviewer 会直接判定没有主动性, 最多 L4。
只有 execution 没有 insight: 大篇幅描述怎么 coding 和 launch, 但说不清为什么只有你发现了这个 gap, 以及你当时的 logic chain, 会被认为深度不足。
跳过数据 rigor: 直接从直觉跳到一个 solution, 没有类似 abandon-log slice 那样的 hypothesis 验证步骤, 显得像是运气或 anecdotal。
故事太顺利: 没有怀疑 hunch 可能错误, 也没有描述如果 hunch 失败会如何止损, 缺少 L5 的 intellectual honesty 和对 risk 的自觉管理。

text: Describe a time when you questioned a traditional approach and proposed something new.
primary_rendered:
QUESTION (Innovation & Strategic Thinking): Describe a time when you questioned a traditional approach and proposed something new.

[PRIMARY] EX-03 | Challenging Sale NDCG Proxy — First Principles Rethinking
  situation: Our search ranking team was optimizing Sale NDCG -- an industry-standard metric -- but I discovered it systematically prioritized cheap items over expensive ones, causing a \$100 necklace to rank below \$5 accessories despite generating far more marketplace value.
  task: I needed to identify the correct optimization proxy and convince the team and stakeholders that the existing industry-standard approach was fundamentally flawed.
  action: - Analyzed the relationship between item price and ranking position; demonstrated that Sale NDCG's conversion-rate weighting created systematic price bias - Proposed GMB (price x sale probability) as the correct optimization target -- this directly measures marketplace value, not just conversion likelihood - Discovered a deeper calibration trap: the model's group-level probabilities looked correct, but individual item scores were insensitive to item-level differences, causing price alone to dominate - Designed a BM25-inspired price transformation with log scaling and per-tranche soft caps -- c
  result: Switching to GMB proxy fundamentally improved ranking behavior. High-quality, authenticated listings saw significant GMB uplift, and the insight that **"proxy selection is the most underestimated ML decision"** became a guiding principle for the entire team's future work.
  evidence_quotes: ["Proxy 选择是 ML 项目里最被低估的决策", "100 刀首饰的 conversion rate 可以高于 5 刀商品的 5 倍", "问题不在于模型选型，而在于 pointwise 框架本身的建模假设是错的"]
  cn_elevator_pitch: 发现 Sale NDCG 系统性偏向低价商品——$5 配饰排在 $100 项链前面；提出 GMB (price x sale probability) 作为正确 proxy，揭示 calibration 陷阱 | KEY FACTS: Sale NDCG 价格偏差 | GMB proxy 替代 | calibration 陷阱 | "proxy 选择是最被低估的 ML 决策"

OTHER LINKED STORIES (context only, 不必引用):
- EX-07 | Relevance Dataset Bias — Challenging the Self-Fulfilling Prophecy: 团队数月争论 relevance filtering 是否有效，发现评估数据集只含 converted results 形成 self-fulfilling prophecy；识别三大根因说服 stakeholders 转向 problem formulation | KEY FACTS: self-fulfillin
- BLOG-04 | Goal Tracking Reform: Honest Metrics Over Cosmetic Delivery: 团队 goal tracking 暗中奖励失败——改名、re-scope、rollover 伪装交付率；推动锁定 scope + peer confidence estimates，短期交付率下降反证系统生效 | KEY FACTS: 锁定 goal scope | peer confidence estimates 
- EX-01 | Search Diversity --- Intent Collapse via Item-vs-Page Diagnosis: Hacker Week 自己去找 search ranker 在哪 silently failing -- dashboard 显示健康但 multi-intent query 比如 "pokemon" 90%+ 返回 trading cards，而购买数据显示一半 buyer 要 games / toys / fig

probe_notes.core_signal: 这题本质在问: 能否从 first principles 出发 challenge 行业标准/团队惯例, 并系统性重构 problem frame 而不是 tweak 现有方案。L5 bar 是能把一次 proxy 替换升华为 'proxy selection is the most underestimated ML decision' 并变成团队决策原则, 影响后续所有 ranking 项目。
what_good_looks_like: EX-03 primary 动作: 分析 item price 和 ranking position 的关系, 展示 Sale NDCG 的 conversion-rate weighting 系统性压制高价商品, 用数据让 bias 显性化, 不是凭直觉反对。
提出 GMB (price x sale probability) 作为新 proxy, 直接测量 marketplace value, 对标的不是某个算法而是整个优化目标的定义 -- first principles 的 proxy 替换, 不是 incremental tweak。
揭示第二层 deeper calibration trap: group-level 概率正确但 item-level 不敏感, 导致 price 摇号主导 ranking -- 这让 challenge 从 metric 问题升到 model design 层面, 展示 '我看到了团队没看到的 trap'。
量化结果: 'high-quality, authenticated listings saw significant GMB uplift', 且 lesson 'proxy selection is the most underestimated ML decision' 变成团队 guiding principle, 表明 challenge 产生了 lasting impact。
what_L5_adds: Insight 的 class-level 抽象: 从 'Sale NDCG 有 price bias' 抬到 'proxy selection is the most underestimated ML decision' -- 这是一个可迁移的 design heuristic, 能在未来所有 ML 项目中预判 proxy risk, 是 L5 的 structural thinking。
Org-level 的 boundary 识别: 指出 '问题不在于模型选型, 而在于 pointwise 框架本身的建模假设是错的' -- 不是指责某个模型, 而是问整个 team 的默认 paradigm 是否有盲区, 这是改变团队集体 mental model 的 L5 动作。
说服 stakeholders 时没有依赖 authority, 而是用 price bias 数据和 GMB uplift 建立不可反驳的 evidence chain, 同时不归功于自己 -- 展示的是 L5 的 'influence without authority' 和 credit-sharing 意识。
common_failure_modes: Incremental tweak 伪装成 challenge: '我换了个更好的 loss function' 但没质疑 loss 定义的源头 -- 如果没展示对 industry-standard metric 的根本性 reasoning 为什么错, 那就只是优化, 不是 question。
没有分析 traditional approach 为什么存在并被广泛采用: 跳过 'Sale NDCG 为什么是行业标准' 这一步, 直接提新方案 -- reviewer 会觉得 candidate 缺乏对 existing practice 的 depth 理解, 被扣 'jump to solution'。
结果没有量化到 business 层面: 只说 'model metric 提高了', 没有像 EX-03 那样证明高价优质 listing GMB 提升, 或者没有把 lesson 变成事后可追溯的 decision record -- L5 bar 会扣 'no org-level impact'。
Stakeholder alignment 讲成 solo win: '我发现了问题并自己改了, 然后上线成功' -- 没有展示如何让 PM/其他 ranking 工程师 buy in, 没有提到任何反对声音和如何处理, reviewer 会认为缺乏 cross-team persuasion, 不够 L5。

text: Tell me about a time when you improved an inefficient process.
primary_rendered:
QUESTION (Innovation & Strategic Thinking): Tell me about a time when you improved an inefficient process.

[PRIMARY] EX-12B | Notebook -> ML Platform Migration --- Team Utilization 5% to 40% via Template+Profile Abstraction (Team-Cut of EX-12)
  situation: Research team 靠常驻 Jupyter notebook 做 model 开发和 inference pipeline。整个 notebook fleet 几百 GB memory + 大量 CPU footprint 常年 reserved，实际 utilization < 5%。几个 legacy 模型还在本地用 R native boosting 包 (gbm 类) 训练 — 没 refresh 通路，也 scale 不到 serving traffic。组里有个公开的开放问题：researcher / DS 到底能不能 ship 可部署的 production-grade 系统。
  task: 把 team 从 ad-hoc notebook 环境迁到成熟的 ML platform，不能牺牲 research velocity；同时正面回应那句"DS can't ship production"的 skepticism。我不是 platform owner — 得靠 RS ↔ Infra 两边的双向翻译，加上把 researcher 的真实需求 推进 platform roadmap，才能让这次迁移真的落地。
  action: Early call: 把"浪费"变成不可辩驳的事实。我 profile 了整个 notebook fleet 的真实 utilization — <5% 的 CPU/GPU 数字 + idle memory reservation 一起摆在 leadership 和 RS 面前。模糊的"感觉在浪费"变成硬数据。  然后我不从 migration mandate 起手，从 researcher 的痛点起手：kernel 动不动挂、legacy R 模型没 refresh 通路、没有 scale 到 serving 的路径。聊下来发现他们其实很 愿意合作 — 只要替代方案真的 viable。  我把自己放在 RS 和 Infra 之间做双向翻译。Researcher 的真实 workflow requirement 我带进 platform roadmap：HDFS、Spark、internal search engine LnP、debug/scrape tooling 兼容性，一条都不能丢 — 否则 researcher 离开 notebook 就是**直接降能**，那这事没人会签。  然后我 push platform 越过早期的 "Kubernetes + ephemeral Docker pod" scope。我的 论点是：要让 RS 既能做 research 又能直接 s
  result: 团队 CPU/GPU utilization 从 <5% 抬到 ~40%（SRE 资源监控测量），释放出的 capacity 被其他 workload 接走。40% 其实是我们 workload shape 的现实天花板 — 每轮 process 几百 GB 数据，I/O + memory 要按 peak read 阶段配，data loading 期间 CPU 必然 idle；在 load / train 阶段动态 re-allocation 落地之前 40% 已经到位，team 非常满意。  迁移顺带解锁了一批 notebook 时代拿不到的底层能力：自动 model versioning、core metric + 历史 weight 一键对比、实时 CPU/GPU 诊断便于 failure mitigation。更关键的 是，它把"DS 能不能 ship production"从组
  cn_elevator_pitch: 研究团队 notebook fleet 几百 GB memory reserved 但 utilization < 5%；几个 legacy R boosting 模型 (gbm 类) 无 refresh 通路、scale 不到 serving。先把 <5% 的 profile 数据摆在 leadership 和 RS 面前把"浪费"变成事实，再从 researcher 痛点起手做 RS↔Infra 双向翻译，把 HDFS/Spark/LnP/debug tooling 需求推进 platform roadmap；然后 push platform 越过 k8s + ephemeral pod 

OTHER LINKED STORIES (context only, 不必引用):
- EX-15 | Model Deprecation Incident --- Reframing Conflict into a Governance Pattern: 我自己的 traffic dashboard 盲区漏掉了 hardcoded 调用，下线 legacy model 后 3-4 个 Query Understanding pipeline 被 block；不争流程对错先吃 rollback，一周内全部 unblock 换到 credibility，再把 "谁必须迁移"
- BLOG-04 | Goal Tracking Reform: Honest Metrics Over Cosmetic Delivery: 团队 goal tracking 暗中奖励失败——改名、re-scope、rollover 伪装交付率；推动锁定 scope + peer confidence estimates，短期交付率下降反证系统生效 | KEY FACTS: 锁定 goal scope | peer confidence estimates 
- EX-05 | Relevance Filtering: Deployment Feasibility Under Latency Constraints: 作为唯一 MLE 发现 XGBoost 模型 +10% latency 远超 <=1% 预算；三路方案中两路失败，最终 cheap rejection + early exit 组合达标 | KEY FACTS: +10% latency vs <=1% 预算 | cheap rejection + early exi

probe_notes.core_signal: 这题本质在问: 能否 diagnose inefficiency 的 root cause (不只是 symptom), 并设计一个改变了约束条件的 solution, 而不是在执行层打补丁。L5 bar 是能从个人 annoyance 抽象出 team/org-level 的 structural gap, 并以跨职能协调者的身份推动 adoption。
what_good_looks_like: 将 inefficiency 翻译成不可辩驳的 data: EX-12B primary 动作是把 '感觉在浪费' 变成 低于 5% CPU/GPU utilization 的 profiling 数据 -- 消除了 ambiguity, 让 decision 从 opinion war 变成 resource discussion。
Solution 不是 push mandate, 而是 align incentives: 从 researcher 的痛点 (kernel crash, 无 refresh 通路, no scalability) 起手, 证明替代方案不降能, 而不是从 '我们必须迁移' 起手。
Explicit cross-function bridge: 把自己定位在 RS 和 Infra 之间的翻译者, 将 HDFS/Spark/LnP/debug tooling 兼容性需求推进 platform roadmap, 而不是单方面要求 researcher 改变行为。
量化结果 + 承认天花板: utilization 从 低于 5% 抬到 ~40%, 同时明确指出 40% 是 workload shape 的现实天花板 -- 既展示了 impact, 又避免 overclaim, 是 L5 级的 honesty。
what_L5_adds: Frame-level shift: 没有把低效归咎于 'researcher 太懒/团队太不 discipline', 而是看清了 tooling 缺口让 researcher 无法 ship production -- 这就是从个人行为归因抬到系统设计缺陷, 是 L5 的系统视角。
Org-level impact: 落地后不仅解了自己的 team, 还隐性回答了 'DS 能不能 ship production' 这个跨组的 credibility 问题, 直接改写了团队在整个组织中的 positioning。
双向翻译中的 self-awareness: 清晰知道自己不是 platform owner, 必须通过 influence 而非 authority 推进需求, 同时能 empathy 两边的真实 constraints, 而不是只站一边喊话。
common_failure_modes: Junior 答案: '我做了一个 script/alias/config 省了自己 10 分钟' -- 只有个人效率, 没有系统改进, reviewer 直接判 L4 以下。
只改 symptom 不改 constraint: 比如 push researcher 关 notebook 或写 guideline, 但没有提供 viable alternative -- 这等于是把 pain 转嫁, reviewer 会问 '你能保证 adoption 吗?' 没有就扣分。
没有 quantify before/after: 只有 '变快了/变好了' 没有具体数字 (5% -> 40%) -- reviewer 无法 measure scope, 会怀疑 impact 很小。
Overclaim without boundary: 声称彻底解决了所有浪费, 没有承认 40% 是天花板 -- L5 需要有认清极限的 maturity, 强行神话结果会崩掉 credibility。

text: Walk me through a difficult technical decision you had to make.
primary_rendered:
QUESTION (Problem Solving & Data-Driven Decisions): Walk me through a difficult technical decision you had to make.

[PRIMARY] EX-05 | Relevance Filtering: Deployment Feasibility Under Latency Constraints
  situation: As tech lead and sole MLE on a relevance filtering project, my team spent two months building a high-accuracy XGBoost model with thousands of trees. At deployment time, we discovered the model added +10% latency overhead -- completely unacceptable against our <=1% budget.
  task: Find a model architecture that met the strict <=1% latency constraint while maintaining acceptable filtering accuracy -- and ensure it actually worked end-to-end in production.
  action: Beat 1 -- Tried three paths, two died. I laid out three approaches: early exit (truncate tree evaluation at convergence depth ~600 trees), feature-pruned small model (retrain with only top-importance features), and cheap rejection (lightweight model rejects obvious cases, passes hard cases to full model). Feature-pruned model lost too much accuracy -- eliminated. Early exit alone landed right at the latency boundary with no safety margin.  Beat 2 -- Key insight: most requests don't need the big model. I went back to the production traffic distribution and noticed something others hadn't focuse
  result: Shipped the feature meeting the <=1% latency target. GMB on null/low-intent queries improved +4-6%. The cheap rejection + early exit pattern was later reused for two other model deployments. The silent failure lesson led me to establish a new practice: before any launch, run an end-to-end payload stress test verifying that model outputs are received intact at every downstream stage -- not just 'ca
  evidence_quotes: ["Over-invested in deep models (thousands of trees) before confronting latency budgets — as sole MLE I should have set the deployment envelope first", "Engineering deployability is the real constraint — fancy ideas fail when the underlying system relies on heavy caching or offline precomputation"]
  cn_elevator_pitch: 作为唯一 MLE 发现 XGBoost 模型 +10% latency 远超 <=1% 预算；三路方案中两路失败，最终 cheap rejection + early exit 组合达标 | KEY FACTS: +10% latency vs <=1% 预算 | cheap rejection + early exit | +4-6% GMB on null/low-intent | end-to-end payload 验证新实践

OTHER LINKED STORIES (context only, 不必引用):
- EX-03 | Challenging Sale NDCG Proxy — First Principles Rethinking: 发现 Sale NDCG 系统性偏向低价商品——$5 配饰排在 $100 项链前面；提出 GMB (price x sale probability) 作为正确 proxy，揭示 calibration 陷阱 | KEY FACTS: Sale NDCG 价格偏差 | GMB proxy 替代 | calibratio
- BLOG-01 | Brand Recall: Influence -- Changing the Researcher-Engineer Dynamic: Researcher 把品牌召回模型"甩墙"过来，缓存需求超现有 infra 一个量级；通过 joint 压缩迭代打破 adversarial 动态，共创 productionization checklist 成团队首个 model-to-prod 标准 | KEY FACTS: 数千万 cache 条目 vs 百万
- EX-20 | Seller Risk Modeling Fairness --- Ethical Dilemma and Escalation: 发现 seller risk model 系统性惩罚新卖家——零交易历史 = 高风险分，形成"永远无法建立信誉"的恶性循环；研究 PayPal 案例 + 平台责任法律框架，推动从 seller-only 转向 seller-listing cross-modeling，经法务确认后落地 | KEY FACTS: 新卖家
- EX-21 | Tech Debt Balance --- Declarative Artifactory Proof of Concept: 新功能依赖团队 declarative artifactory 系统但长期 delay 无 timeline；深入研究发现核心价值是 JSON ranking rule expression generation，blocker 是周边 infra；用内部 caching 系统做 storage，功能按时交付且后续迁移
- EX-09B | Conversational Search Privacy: Proxy Item Generation Eliminates Raw Query Leakage Risk (Privacy-Cut of EX-09): 在 LLM 对话搜索 design 阶段提出 query rewrite 路径会让用户原始 query 流入下游 log/训练数据的 privacy 风险；与 team 共同 develop proxy item 生成路径，让原始 query 永不流入下游，并把 privacy 优势写入 design doc | KE

probe_notes.core_signal: 这题本质在问: 在约束冲突 (accuracy vs latency) 下能否展示 data-driven 的决策逻辑/tradeoff 的显式比较, 以及最终决策的 org-level 影响。L5 bar 是决策不只解决当前问题, 还沉淀为可迁移的实践或 pattern, 并且能反思自己 over-investment 的盲点。
what_good_looks_like: EX-05 primary 动作: 回到生产流量分布, 注意到 'most requests don't need the big model', 据此提出 cheap rejection + early exit 组合 -- 这是 traffic-distribution 驱动的 insight, 不是凭空试出来的。
决策路径显式呈现: 三条路径 (early exit / feature-pruned / cheap rejection) 中两条已死, 哪条触达 latency 边界无余量, 哪条因 accuracy 被淘汰, 让 reviewer 看到你在有限 option 中做 constrained optimization。
量化的业务影响和可迁移性: 不只是 'latency 达标', 而是 'GMB on null/low-intent queries +4-6%' 并且 'pattern later reused for two other model deployments'。
反思落脚在 preventive pattern: 不是 '下次早测 latency', 而是建立了 'end-to-end payload stress test 验证模型输出在每一个下游节点完整到达' 的 launch 前新实践, 这是一次 concrete process shift。
what_L5_adds: 从 single fix 到 reusable pattern: cheap rejection + early exit 后来被另外两个模型部署复用, 这说明决策影响力超出了单点项目, 是 L5 的 org-level multiplier。
从技术决策到流程补强: 补的不是 '加一个 check', 而是 design 阶段的 deployability envelope 前置, 以及 launch 阶段的跨链路 integrity validation, 这是 structural prevention。
Self-awareness on over-investment: 作为 sole MLE 承认 'I should have set the deployment envelope first', 这种对 expertise-sunk-cost 的清醒是 L5 区别于 L4 的单点技术执行。
common_failure_modes: 只描述做了什么而没有 tradeoff tension: '我们试了 A 不行换 B 成功了' -- 缺少 3 条路径中 2 条为何死掉的具体分析, reviewer 听不出决策难度, 降级。
没有数据锚点: 不给出 '10% latency vs 1% budget' / 'GMB +4-6%' 这类量级感, 变成 pure anecdote, 无法验证 scope。
把成功归结为偶然灵感: '然后我突然想到 cheap rejection' -- 没讲 insight 是来自 traffic distribution 分析, 缺乏 data-driven 痕迹, 会丢 point。
反思停留在战术: '下次要早点 profile latency' -- 没有落地为 team-usable 的流程变更 (如 payload stress test), 停留在个人悔过, L5 bar 够不到。

text: Describe a time when you used data to make a key decision.
primary_rendered:

[PRIMARY] EX-01 | Search Diversity --- Intent Collapse via Item-vs-Page Diagnosis
  situation: During Hacker Week I went looking for where our search ranker was failing silently. Standard dashboards looked healthy. But multi-intent queries like "pokemon" returned 90%+ trading cards, while purchase data showed half the buyers wanted games, toys, or figures. The dashboard was fine because the dominant-intent users were fine. The missing half was invisible.
  task: No one had assigned this. One week to go from a hunch to a defensible diagnosis plus a working prototype -- or drop it. The framing mattered more than the fix. If I couldn't name precisely why the ranker produced homogeneous pages, nobody downstream would fund a multi-intent solution on top of a hea
  action: First pass: abandon-log slice. Sorted queries by post-impression drop-off and looked for the pattern. Hundreds of high-volume multi-intent queries collapsed the same way -- one product type crowded out every other valid interpretation. Not a bug on any single query. A systematic bias.  Root-cause call: the ranker scored each item in isolation. It had no mechanism to reason about the page. When the top candidates all looked alike, the page looked alike -- by design. Item-level scoring was producing page-level homogeneity, and no amount of per-item tuning would fix it. The gap was structural, no
  result: The prototype survived review and grew past Hacker Week. Compounded across verticals into 200M+ annualized impact over multiple years. The methodology was later written up at SIGIR. probe_notes.core_signal: 这题本质在问: 你如何用数据诊断一个 observable 信号 (或信号缺失), 并用该诊断做出一个 key decision -- 而这个 decision 改变了后续方向 (不是 just 'used data to answer a question')。L5 bar 是能挑战现有指标的健康假象, 自己定义正确的诊断数据切片, 并将发现上升为结构性 insight。
what_good_looks_like: 展示数据洞察的三段式: (1) 发现仪表盘健康但实际 client behavior 不一致; EX-01 primary 动作: 'abandon-log slice 发现上百个 high-volume multi-intent query 同样 collapse', 证明是系统性偏差。
决策不是被数据推动的, 而是从数据主动推断 root-cause; EX-01 的 root-cause call: 'item-level scoring produces page-level homogeneity' -- 这是从诊断到结构性决策的跳跃。
包含具体的 metrics 对比: EX-01 中仪表盘显示 '健康' vs. 购买数据 '50% 买家想要 games/toys/figures, 但页面 90% trading cards' -- 两个 data source 的张力催生了决策。
决策产生实际影响: EX-01 原型活过 Hacker Week, 跨垂直领域带来 200M+ annualized impact, 方法论被 SIGIR 论文收录 -- 证明决策的重要性。
what_L5_adds: 挑战被广泛认可的指标: 不认为 'dashboard 健康' 就是健康, 而是主动诊断系统在哪些地方 failing silently -- 这是 L5 的 diagnostic leadership。
将发现提炼为可复用的设计原则: 'item-level scoring creates page-level homogeneity' 是一个能够改变未来 ranker 设计的 pattern, 而非一次性的 bug fix。
自驱动 (self-assigned) 的 ownership: 没有 task master, 自己发现/自己推动/跨团队落地 -- L5 期望的主动性边界超出了直接经理分配的 scope。
common_failure_modes: 数据使用太 shallow: 只报告一个 A/B test 结果, 没有解释为什么数据指向那个决策, 也没有诊断 'why' -- reviewer 会问 '那你除了看到了数字还做了什么?'。
决策只是优化现有系统: 比如 '我用数据把 recall 提高了 5%' -- 这种答案缺少结构性 insight, L5 需要的是改变了 framing 的决策, 比如挑战现有 objective。
把数据洞察归因于算法而不是自己的诊断: '模型自动发现了 pattern' -- 这没有展示自己的 problem solving, ownership 被算法代替。
没有展示 counter-evidence or 对照: 好答案需要两个 data source 的张力; 若只有单一数据源 '某个指标下降了, 所以做 X', 显得决策无分歧, 也不难。
